mainTopic: Feeding hired workers, and the אגדה of אברהם's hospitality to the three מלאכים: his meal compared with שלמה's, the three calves, the rewards to his descendants, and the visit after his מילה.
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining the משנה: an employer who promises food to his workers has taken on more than the usual. רבי יוחנן בן מתיא told his son that even a feast like שלמה's would not cover such a promise, because the workers are children of אברהם, יצחק and יעקב. The גמרא asks how אברהם's three calves could beat שלמה's enormous daily menu, and answers that per person אברהם gave far more. Next the גמרא explains words in the פסוקים: what made שלמה's birds 'fattened', which animals are the finest, and how רב finds three calves in 'בן בקר רך וטוב'. It defends that reading against challenges and explains that the three calves let אברהם serve each guest a tongue with mustard. Then come teachings about reward: רב says ה׳ repaid אברהם's descendants in the same way he served his guests, either personally or through a messenger, while רבי חמא ברבי חנינא lines up the rewards differently. The amud ends with the story of the hot day after אברהם's מילה, the identity of the three מלאכים and their jobs, and a question about why the מלאכים agreed at once to stay with אברהם but not with לוט. The answer to that question comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Promising food means more, and the story of רבי יוחנן בן מתיא
steps.stepSummary: An employer who promises food has committed to more than the normal standard. רבי יוחנן בן מתיא told his son that even a feast like שלמה's would not satisfy such an open promise to the children of the אבות.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he promised them food, he has taken on more. There is also a story about רבי יוחנן בן מתיא. He told his son to go hire workers, and the son promised them food. His father said: even a feast like שלמה's would not fulfill that promise, because they are children of אברהם, יצחק and יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its filled-in reading of the משנה: an employer who promises food has obligated himself to extra. It then brings a story that supports this rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the local custom decides what workers get. But if the employer goes out of his way to promise food without limits, he has raised the bar. רבי יוחנן בן מתיא shows how high that bar can go: for descendants of the אבות, an open-ended promise of food has almost no ceiling.

keyTerms.meaning: He promised them food as part of the deal

steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that an open-ended promise to workers is read generously, and that Jewish workers deserve to be treated with great dignity.

phrases.english: he has increased [his obligation] to them.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַעֲשֶׂה נָמֵי בְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן מַתְיָא
phrases.english: And there was also an incident with Rabbi Yochanan ben Matya
who said to his son:
Go out and hire workers for us.
He went and promised them food.
And when he came to his father,
he said to him: My son,
even if you make for them
a feast like that of Solomon in his time,
you would not have fulfilled your obligation to them,
for they are the children of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַעֲשֶׂה נָמֵי בְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן מַתְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the גמרא's filled-in reading of the משנה, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An employer who promises food without limits has obligated himself beyond the local norm. For descendants of the אבות, even a royal feast would not be enough.

steps.title: Was אברהם's meal really greater than שלמה's?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the story. It assumes the father meant that the workers deserve אברהם's kind of meal, and it quotes the huge daily menu of שלמה. Two אמוראים add that even the massive flour amounts were only for side uses in the kitchen.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean אברהם's feast was better than שלמה's? The פסוק lists שלמה's daily food: huge amounts of flour, many oxen, a hundred sheep, wild animals and fattened birds. רב said the flour was just for the cooks' dough. רבי יצחק said it was for pot-pudding.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the story. It is building a picture of how enormous שלמה's feasts were, so it can compare them with אברהם's simple meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling the workers 'children of אברהם' suggests they deserve a meal like the one אברהם served his guests, one that outdoes שלמה's. But the פסוק describes a staggering amount of food. רב and רבי יצחק make the picture even bigger: all that flour was only for side jobs in the kitchen, not the main meal.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (a question about what follows from a statement)
But isn't it written? (opens a challenge from a פסוק)
A very large measure of dry goods
The cooks' worked dough, a side use of flour in the kitchen
Pot-pudding, a mixture cooked in the pot

phrases.english: Is that to say that the feast of Abraham our father
is greater than Solomon's?
But isn't it written:
"And Solomon's bread for one day was

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלֹשִׁים כֹּר סֹלֶת וְשִׁשִּׁים כֹּר קָמַח.
phrases.english: thirty kor of fine flour and sixty kor of meal;
phrases.notes: מלכים א 5:2–3

phrases.aramaic: עֲשָׂרָה בָּקָר בְּרִאִים וַעֲשָׂרָה בָּקָר רְעִי
phrases.english: ten fat oxen and ten oxen from the pastures,
phrases.notes: The פסוק itself says 'twenty' pasture oxen here.

phrases.english: and a hundred sheep,
besides harts, gazelles and roebucks,
and fattened fowl!"

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר גּוּרְיוֹן בֶּן אֲסִטְיוֹן מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: And Guryon ben Asteyon said in the name of Rav:
These were for the cooks' worked dough.
And Rabbi Yitzchak said:
These were for pot-pudding.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דִּסְעוּדְתָּא דְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עֲדִיפָא מִדִּשְׁלֹמֹה? וְהָכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the implication of רבי יוחנן בן מתיא's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication that אברהם's meal was greater than שלמה's feast.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק shows שלמה's daily food was enormous, and even the flour was only for side uses. How could אברהם's meal be greater?

steps.title: שלמה's thousand wives versus אברהם's three calves
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק adds that each of שלמה's thousand wives prepared this huge feast daily, hoping he would eat with her. By contrast, אברהם served only three calves, which makes the question even sharper.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: שלמה had a thousand wives, and each one made this whole feast at her house every day. Why? Each one thought, 'Maybe he will eat with me today.' But by אברהם it says he took 'a calf, tender and good,' and רב explained that this means only three calves!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps building its challenge. It multiplies שלמה's feast by a thousand and sets it against אברהם's modest three calves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the gap looks huge: a thousand royal feasts every day against just three calves. רב's reading of the three words in the פסוק (בן בקר, רך, טוב) gives the number three. The question is now sharp: how can אברהם's meal be called greater?

keyTerms.meaning: A calf, tender and good (read by רב as three calves)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak said:
Solomon had a thousand wives,

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת עָשְׂתָה לוֹ בְּבֵיתָה כָּךְ.
phrases.english: and each one made this for him in her house.
phrases.notes: 'This' means the entire giant menu from the פסוק, every single day.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ סְבוּרָה שֶׁמָּא אֶצְלִי סוֹעֵד הַיּוֹם,
phrases.english: This one thought: Perhaps he will dine with me today,

phrases.aramaic: וְזוֹ סְבוּרָה שֶׁמָּא אֶצְלִי סוֹעֵד הַיּוֹם.
phrases.english: and that one thought: Perhaps he will dine with me today.
Whereas regarding Abraham it is written:
"And Abraham ran to the herd
and took a calf, tender and good."
phrases.notes: בראשית 18:7

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
"A calf" is one,
"tender" is two, "and good" is three!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and sharpens the challenge from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that אברהם's meal outranks שלמה's.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שלמה's feast was prepared a thousand times daily, while אברהם served only three calves. The numbers seem to show the opposite.

steps.title: Per person, אברהם's meal was greater
steps.stepSummary: אברהם served three oxen to three guests, while שלמה's food was for the entire nation of יהודה and ישראל. So for each person, אברהם's meal was far richer.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, אברהם served three oxen to three men. Here, שלמה's food was for all of ישראל and יהודה, who were as many as the sand by the sea.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It compares how much each guest received instead of the total amount of food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge compared total amounts. The answer looks at portions: a whole ox for each of אברהם's three guests, against food spread over a huge nation. Measured per person, אברהם's hospitality wins, so רבי יוחנן בן מתיא's statement stands.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: An open promise of food to workers is read generously. The children of אברהם deserve hospitality like his, which per person was greater than even שלמה's royal feasts.
steps.confusionAlert: The question is not how much food in total, but how much each person got. שלמה's food was spread over the whole nation, while אברהם gave one ox per guest.

phrases.english: There, three oxen for three men;
phrases.notes: The three men are the three guests (angels) who visited אברהם.

phrases.english: here, for all of Israel and Judah,
as it is said:
"Judah and Israel were many,
like the sand that is by the sea."
phrases.notes: מלכים א 4:20

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם תְּלָתָא תּוֹרֵי לִתְלָתָא גַּבְרֵי, הָכָא לְכׇל יִשְׂרָאֵל וִיהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised in steps 2–3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing the comparison from total quantity to amount per person.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שלמה's feast was far greater because its total amount was enormous.
steps.terutzMaskana: Per guest, אברהם's meal (an ox per person) was greater than שלמה's, which fed the entire nation.

steps.title: What does 'fatted fowl' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the phrase ברבורים אבוסים in שלמה's menu means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'fatted fowl'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask about one phrase from שלמה's daily menu, quoted earlier. This question sets up the three answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אבוסים can mean 'fattened', but it does not say how the birds got fat. The גמרא wants to know what made שלמה's birds special.

keyTerms.meaning: Fowl; a kind of fine bird

phrases.english: What is 'fatted fowl'?
phrases.notes: This phrase is from שלמה's menu in מלכים א 5:3, quoted earlier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to a phrase from שלמה's menu (Step 2) to explain it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of אבוסים in the description of שלמה's birds.

steps.title: Three explanations of the fattened animals
steps.stepSummary: רב says the birds were force-fed. שמואל says they were naturally fat. רבי יוחנן says the animals were never forced to work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב says: they were force-fed. שמואל says: they were fat on their own. רבי יוחנן says: they brought an ox from its pasture that was never forced to work, and a hen from its coop that was never forced to lay.
steps.whatsHappening: Three אמוראים each explain what made שלמה's animals so fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב reads אבוסים as active: someone fattened them by force. שמואל reads it as a natural state: they were fat by nature. רבי יוחנן widens the point to both ox and hen: the quality came from animals that were never worn out by work.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב: שֶׁאוֹבְסִים אוֹתָן בְּעַל כׇּרְחָן.
phrases.english: Rav said: that they fatten them against their will.
And Shmuel said: that they are fat and stay that way on their own.
And Rabbi Yochanan said:
They bring an ox from its pasture that was never forced,
phrases.notes: He means it was never forced to work.

phrases.english: and a hen from its coop that was never forced.
phrases.notes: Here it means the hen was never pushed to lay eggs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: שֶׁאוֹבְסִים אוֹתָן בְּעַל כׇּרְחָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Three views: force-fed (רב), naturally fat (שמואל), never forced to work (רבי יוחנן).

steps.title: The choicest animal and the choicest bird
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the best of the animals is the ox, and the best of the birds is the hen.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: the choicest of animals is the ox, and the choicest of birds is the hen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related statement from רבי יוחנן, ranking the best meats.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His last statement mentioned an ox and a hen, so the גמרא adds his general rule about them: these are the finest meats of all.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
The choicest of the animals is the ox,
the choicest of the birds is the hen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related teaching of the same רבי יוחנן about ox and hen.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ox is the best animal and the hen is the best bird.

steps.title: Which hen is the best
steps.stepSummary: אמימר describes the best hen: a fat black hen living among the wine vats, so heavy it can hardly walk.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: a fattened black hen found among the wine vats, which cannot even step the length of a reed.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר explains exactly which kind of hen רבי יוחנן meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every hen is 'the best'. It is one that eats so much grape waste near the wine presses that it becomes too fat to move.

keyTerms.meaning: A reed (a short measure of length)

phrases.english: Ameimar said:
a black hen, a fattened one,
that is found among the wine vats,
that cannot step the length of a reed.
phrases.notes: It eats so many grape seeds that it is too fat to walk even a short distance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the hen of רבי יוחנן's statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The best hen is the fat black one from among the wine vats.

steps.title: אברהם served three calves
steps.stepSummary: רב reads three calves out of the פסוק: בן בקר is one, רך is two, וטוב is three.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And to the herd אברהם ran'. רב יהודה said in the name of רב: 'a calf' is one, 'tender' is two, 'and good' is three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to אברהם and shows the source that he served three animals. Steps 3 and 4 relied on this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each describing word in the פסוק is read as one more animal. This gives three calves, one for each guest.

phrases.english: 'And to the herd Abraham ran',
phrases.notes: בראשית 18:7

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
'A calf' is one,
'tender' is two,
'and good' is three.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וְאֶל הַבָּקָר רָץ אַבְרָהָם״, אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side topic of choice animals and gives the source for אברהם's three calves.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק hints at three calves.

steps.title: Maybe it was only one calf
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: maybe 'tender and good' just describes one calf, the way people normally talk.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it was one, as people say: 'tender and good'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב: normal speech uses several describing words for one thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People say 'soft and good' about a single item. So the extra words may just describe one calf and not add more calves.

phrases.english: But say it was one,
as people say: 'tender and good'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's reading in Step 9.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Everyday speech uses several describing words for one item, so the פסוק may mean only one calf.

steps.title: The extra 'and' shows a teaching
steps.stepSummary: If it meant one calf, the תורה would write 'tender, good'. The extra 'and' shows there is more to learn.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let it write 'tender, good'. Why 'and good'? Learn from this that it comes to teach something.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the little word 'and' is extra and points to another calf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plain description would not need the ו. Since the פסוק adds it, the word 'good' must be adding a new item, not just describing.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching drawn from the wording of a פסוק

phrases.english: If so, let it write 'tender, good',
what is 'and good'?
phrases.notes: The point is the extra letter ו, meaning 'and', which suggests adding something.

phrases.english: Learn from this that it is for a teaching.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the פסוק's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Tender and good' is just normal speech for one calf.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra ו shows the פסוק is adding at least one more calf.

steps.title: Maybe it was only two calves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: the extra 'and' only proves one more calf, so say there were two.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say two!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks: the ו adds one calf, but how do we get to three?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only וטוב has the extra 'and'. So maybe רך is just a description, and the total is two calves.

phrases.english: Say two!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the answer of Step 11 to only two calves.
steps.kashyaTarget: The step from 'more than one' to 'three'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ו proves only one extra calf, which makes two, not three.

steps.title: If 'good' teaches, 'tender' teaches too
steps.stepSummary: Since 'good' is used for a teaching, 'tender' must also be used for a teaching. That makes three calves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since 'good' is for a teaching, 'tender' is also for a teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that once we see the describing words are counting calves, 'tender' counts one as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ו showed that these describing words are not plain description. So 'tender' is read the same way, and the total is three. This backs up Step 4: three calves for three guests.
steps.whatToRemember: רב reads three calves from בן בקר, רך and וטוב. The extra ו proves the words are for a teaching, and 'tender' follows 'good'. This is the source for אברהם serving three animals, one per guest.

phrases.english: Since 'good' is for a teaching,
'tender' is also for a teaching.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading neighboring words the same way
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only 'good' adds a calf, so there are two.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Tender' is read like 'good', so there are three calves.

steps.title: The verse says 'it', so maybe there was only one calf
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר עולא (or רב הושעיא, or רב נתן ברבי הושעיא) challenges רב: the פסוק says the young man prepared 'it', which sounds like a single calf.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר עולא raised an objection (some say it was רב הושעיא, and some say רב נתן son of רבי הושעיא): The פסוק says, 'And he gave it to the young man, and he hurried to prepare it.' That sounds like only one calf.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge against רב's three calves. It uses a word in the פסוק that seems to point to only one calf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אֹתוֹ ('it') is singular. If there were three calves, we might expect the פסוק to say 'them'. So the plain wording seems to argue against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: raises an objection, usually from a source
and some say (another name for who said it)

phrases.english: Rabba bar Ulla raises an objection,
and some say it was Rav Hoshaya,
and some say it was Rav Natan son of Rabbi Hoshaya:
"And he gave it to the young man,
and he hurried to prepare it"
phrases.notes: בראשית 18:7. The point is the word 'it'. It is singular, so it sounds like one calf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 13 proved three calves from the extra words, this step attacks that conclusion from a different word in the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's reading that there were three calves.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The singular אֹתוֹ suggests only one animal was prepared.

steps.title: Each calf went to a different servant
steps.stepSummary: The answer: אברהם gave each calf to its own servant, so for each servant the פסוק correctly says 'it'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Each and every calf, he gave it to one servant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. There were three calves, but each one was handed to a different servant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'it' is true from each servant's side, since each servant prepared one calf. So the singular word fits perfectly with three calves.

phrases.english: Each and every one
he gave it to one young man.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל חַד וְחַד יַהֲבֵיהּ לְנַעַר חַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the singular word as applying to each servant separately.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'It' means there was only one calf.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'It' refers to the one calf each servant received; there were still three in total.

steps.title: The serving verse also says one calf
steps.stepSummary: A second challenge: the next פסוק describes אברהם serving 'the calf' in the singular, together with the butter and milk.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And he took butter and milk, and the calf that he had prepared, and placed it before them.' Here too it sounds like one calf.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another challenge from the next פסוק. It describes the serving with a single calf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer explained the preparing: each servant had one calf. But this פסוק is about serving the guests, and it still mentions 'the calf' in the singular, so the first answer does not cover it.
steps.confusionAlert: There is no word like 'they asked' here. Just quoting the פסוק is the challenge, because it again speaks of only one calf.

phrases.english: "And he took butter and milk
phrases.notes: בראשית 18:8

phrases.english: and the calf that he had prepared,
and he placed it before them"

steps.triggerLanguage: וַיִּקַּח חֶמְאָה וְחָלָב וּבֶן הַבָּקָר אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 15 explained the preparing stage, this challenges the serving stage.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that three calves were served.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even when serving, the פסוק speaks of a single calf.

steps.title: He served each calf as soon as it was ready
steps.stepSummary: The answer: as each calf was finished, אברהם brought that one right away. That is why the פסוק speaks of one at a time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whichever one arrived first, he brought it before them first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the calves were served one by one as each was ready, not all at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes each serving separately, and each serving was one calf. So the singular wording fits three calves served one after another.

keyTerms.meaning: the first, the first (each one in turn)

steps.whatToRemember: Both 'it' challenges are answered by looking at each calf on its own: one per servant, and one served at a time. רב's three calves still stand.

phrases.english: that whichever one arrived first,
he brought it before them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the singular as describing serving in stages.
steps.terutzMaskana: Three calves were served, one at a time as each became ready.

steps.title: Why would three guests need three calves?
steps.stepSummary: Now that we accept three calves, the גמרא asks why so much was needed when one calf could feed three guests.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need three? One should be enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the three calves and now asks for the reason. It sets up the answer that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack on רב's reading anymore. It asks what the purpose was, since one calf has more than enough meat for three people.

phrases.english: And why do I need three?
One should be enough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Once three calves are established, the גמרא asks why.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason אברהם prepared three calves when one would have been enough.

steps.title: Three tongues with mustard
steps.stepSummary: רב חנן בר רבא explains that אברהם wanted to serve each guest a tongue with mustard, a special delicacy. Each calf has only one tongue.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנן בר רבא said: In order to feed them three tongues with mustard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: three calves were needed to give each guest a tongue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat was not the issue. The goal was a fancy dish, tongue with mustard, for every guest. Since a calf has one tongue, three guests needed three calves.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥanan bar Rava said:
In order to feed them
three tongues with mustard.
phrases.notes: Each calf has one tongue, so one tongue per guest takes three calves.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא כְּדֵי לְהַאֲכִילָן שָׁלֹשׁ לְשׁוֹנוֹת בְּחַרְדָּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Three calves were needed to serve each of the three guests a tongue with mustard.

steps.title: Never change from the local custom
steps.stepSummary: רבי תנחום בר חנילאי teaches that a person should follow the custom of the place he is in: משה did not eat in heaven, and the מלאכים ate when they came down to earth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי תנחום בר חנילאי said: A person should never act differently from the local custom. משה went up on high and did not eat bread, and the מלאכי השרת came down below and ate bread.
steps.whatsHappening: Connected to the meal אברהם served, the גמרא brings a lesson about fitting in with local custom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In heaven nobody eats, so משה did not eat. On earth people eat, so the מלאכים ate. Each one acted the way people act in the place where he was.

keyTerms.meaning: he should not change / act differently

steps.whyThisMatters: This became a well-known guide for behavior: when you are in a place, follow how people there act.

phrases.english: Rabbi Tanḥum bar Ḥanilai said:

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם אַל יְשַׁנֶּה אָדָם מִן הַמִּנְהָג,
phrases.english: A person should never act differently from the custom,
for Moses went up on high
and did not eat bread,
the ministering angels came down below
and ate bread.
phrases.notes: These are the guests in אברהם's tent.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם בַּר חֲנִילַאי לְעוֹלָם אַל יְשַׁנֶּה אָדָם מִן הַמִּנְהָג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the details of the meal to a lesson drawn from the מלאכים eating it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should not act differently from local custom, as shown by משה and the מלאכים.

steps.title: Can angels really eat?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: how can you say the מלאכים actually ate?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And they ate'? Could that enter your mind?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of רבי תנחום's teaching, because מלאכים do not eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מלאכים are spiritual and do not need food. So saying they really ate cannot be correct, and the statement needs fixing.

keyTerms.meaning: could it enter your mind? (that cannot be)

phrases.english: 'And they ate'? Could that enter your mind?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges one phrase in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The words 'and they ate bread' in רבי תנחום's statement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מלאכים do not actually eat, so the statement cannot mean that literally.

steps.title: They only looked like they ate
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the wording: the מלאכים seemed to eat and drink, but did not really.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: they looked as if they were eating and drinking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of the statement so that it makes sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lesson about custom stays the same. The מלאכים still behaved like people on earth by appearing to eat, even though nothing was really eaten.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
they looked like ones who ate and drank.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא נִרְאוּ כְּמִי שֶׁאָכְלוּ וְשָׁתוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the statement.
steps.terutzMaskana: They only appeared to eat and drink, which still fits the lesson about custom.

steps.title: ה׳ repaid אברהם measure for measure
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב: whatever אברהם did for the מלאכים personally, הקדוש ברוך הוא did personally for his children. Whatever אברהם did through a messenger, הקדוש ברוך הוא did for them through a messenger.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Everything that אברהם did for the מלאכי השרת by himself, הקדוש ברוך הוא did for his children by Himself. And everything that אברהם did through a messenger, הקדוש ברוך הוא did for his children through a messenger.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about the reward for אברהם's hospitality. The reward matched exactly how he served.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reward is measure for measure. The parts אברהם did himself were repaid by הקדוש ברוך הוא acting directly for בני ישראל. The parts he gave to a servant were repaid through a messenger.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the effort you personally put into a מצוה matters, not just whether it gets done.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Everything that Abraham did
for the ministering angels by himself,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, did
for his children by Himself.
And everything that Abraham did
through a messenger,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, did
for his children through a messenger.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב כׇּל מַה שֶּׁעָשָׂה אַבְרָהָם לְמַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת בְּעַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching about the reward for אברהם's hospitality.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הקדוש ברוך הוא repaid אברהם's descendants in the same way he served the guests: directly for what he did himself, through a messenger for what he delegated.

steps.title: Matching verses: meat and bread from ה׳
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pairs פסוקים: אברהם ran to the herd himself, and a wind went out from ה׳ bringing meat. אברהם took butter and milk himself, and ה׳ rained bread from heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And אברהם ran to the herd', and on the other side, 'A wind went out from ה׳.' 'And he took butter and milk', and on the other side, 'Behold, I will rain bread for you from heaven.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows examples of רב's rule by pairing what אברהם did himself with what ה׳ did Himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אברהם himself ran for the meat, so ה׳ Himself sent the wind that brought the quail. אברהם himself took the butter and milk, so ה׳ Himself rained down the מן. Both examples are from the 'by himself' half of the rule.
steps.whatToRemember: אברהם's personal effort for his guests was repaid with ה׳'s personal care for בני ישראל in the מדבר: meat (the quail) and bread (the מן).

phrases.english: "And Abraham ran to the herd"
phrases.notes: בראשית 18:7. He did this himself.

phrases.english: "And a wind went out from the Lord."
phrases.notes: במדבר 11:31. That wind brought the quail, meat, to בני ישראל.

phrases.english: "And he took butter and milk"
phrases.notes: בראשית 18:8

phrases.english: "Behold, I will rain down for you
bread from heaven."
phrases.notes: שמות 16:4, about the מן.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶל הַבָּקָר רָץ אַבְרָהָם וְרוּחַ נָסַע מֵאֵת ה׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives examples from the פסוקים for רב's rule in step 23.
steps.raayaObject: רב's rule that what אברהם did himself, ה׳ did Himself for his children.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 18:7-8 paired with במדבר 11:31 and שמות 16:4.

steps.title: More things אברהם did himself, matched by ה׳ acting Himself
steps.stepSummary: Two more pairs of פסוקים show personal acts. אברהם stood over his guests, and ה׳ said He would stand on the rock. אברהם walked with his guests, and ה׳ walked before ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: אברהם 'stood over them under the tree,' and ה׳ said, 'I will stand before you there on the rock.' אברהם 'walked with them to send them off,' and 'ה׳ walked before them by day.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps going with the list of matching פסוקים from step 24. These show more things אברהם did with his own body, which ה׳ then did Himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each pair puts a personal act of אברהם next to a personal act of ה׳. Standing matches standing, and walking matches walking. This adds more proof to רב's rule that personal acts were repaid personally.

keyTerms.meaning: stood over them, waiting on the guests
the rock that gave water in the מדבר
to send them off, walking guests out
walked before them, leading the way

phrases.english: "And he stood over them under the tree"
phrases.notes: בראשית 18:8

phrases.english: "Behold, I will stand before you
there upon the rock, [and so on]"
phrases.notes: שמות 17:6

phrases.english: "And אברהם walked with them to send them off"
phrases.notes: בראשית 18:16

phrases.english: "And ה׳ walked before them by day"
phrases.notes: שמות 13:21

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of matching פסוקים begun in step 24
steps.raayaObject: רב's rule that what אברהם did personally, ה׳ did personally
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 18:8 with שמות 17:6, and בראשית 18:16 with שמות 13:21

steps.title: The water אברהם sent for was repaid through a messenger
steps.stepSummary: אברהם had water brought by someone else. In the same way, ישראל's water came through a messenger, when משה struck the rock.
steps.simpleTranslation: אברהם said, 'Let a little water be brought.' In return: 'You shall strike the rock, and water will come out of it, and the people will drink.'
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא proves the second half of רב's rule. Something אברהם did through a helper was repaid through a helper.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'יֻקַּח' means 'let it be taken,' so אברהם did not fetch the water himself. To match this, the water in the מדבר came through משה hitting the rock, not directly from ה׳. This completes the proof for both parts of רב's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: let it please be taken, by someone else
messenger or agent, the idea behind this pairing

steps.whatToRemember: רב's rule: personal acts of אברהם (bringing meat, bread, standing, walking) were repaid personally by ה׳. The water, which he had brought through someone else, was repaid through משה.

phrases.english: "Let a little water be taken"
phrases.notes: בראשית 18:4. אברהם had someone else bring the water.

phrases.english: "And you shall strike the rock
and water will come out of it, and the people will drink"
phrases.notes: שמות 17:6. משה hits the rock, so he is the messenger here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the proof by showing the messenger half of רב's rule
steps.raayaObject: רב's rule that what אברהם did through a messenger, ה׳ did through a messenger

steps.title: Another opinion: three acts of hospitality earned three rewards
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says that רבי חמא ברבי חנינא, along with a ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל, disagrees with רב. They teach that three acts earned three rewards: the מן, the עמוד הענן, and the באר של מרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: This argues with רבי חמא ברבי חנינא. He said, and the school of רבי ישמעאל taught the same: for three things they earned three things. For 'butter and milk' they earned the מן. For 'he stood over them' they earned the pillar of cloud. For 'let a little water be taken' they earned מרים's well.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that a different teaching disagrees with רב, and then quotes it. This teaching lists three rewards for three of אברהם's acts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב's view, the water came through a messenger, משה striking the rock. Here, the water reward is the באר של מרים, and there is no split between what אברהם did himself and what he did through others. The 'stood' reward is also different: here it is the עמוד הענן, a wordplay on עומד and עמוד.

keyTerms.meaning: the school of רבי ישמעאל taught, quoting a ברייתא
the pillar of cloud that led ישראל
מרים's well, the water source in the מדבר

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי חמא is arguing about whether ישראל were rewarded. Both sides agree on that. The argument is about how the rewards line up, especially the water.

phrases.english: And this argues with רבי חמא son of רבי חנינא.
phrases.notes: 'This' means רב's teaching that we just finished.

phrases.english: For רבי חמא son of רבי חנינא said,
and so the school of רבי ישמעאל taught:
In reward for three, they earned three.
In reward for "butter and milk," they earned the מן;
in reward for "and he stood over them",
they earned the pillar of cloud;
phrases.notes: Notice the wordplay: עומד means 'stood,' and עמוד means 'pillar.'

phrases.english: in reward for "let a little water be taken",
they earned the well of מרים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents a teaching that lines up the rewards differently from רב
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three acts of hospitality earned three rewards: milk and butter earned the מן, standing earned the עמוד הענן, and the water earned the באר של מרים.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows two different ways of reading how ה׳ repaid אברהם: רב splits personal acts from messenger acts, while this teaching does not.

steps.title: The angels respond to being asked to wash their feet
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי ברבי ישמעאל teaches what the מלאכים said to אברהם. They asked if he suspected them of being Arabs who worship the dust of their feet, and pointed out that ישמעאל had already come from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Let a little water be taken, and wash your feet.' רבי ינאי son of רבי ישמעאל said: They said to him, 'Do you suspect us of being Arabs, who bow down to the dust of their feet? ישמעאל has already come out from you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new comment on the same פסוק. It explains the reason behind 'wash your feet' and how the guests reacted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The guests understood that the washing was meant to remove dust that some people worship. They answered that they were not like those Arabs. They added that such people already came from אברהם himself: his own son ישמעאל behaves this way.
steps.whatToRemember: The water אברהם offered was to wash off dust that some people worshipped. The מלאכים reacted to being suspected of that.

phrases.english: "Let a little water be taken, and wash your feet"
phrases.notes: בראשית 18:4

phrases.english: רבי ינאי son of רבי ישמעאל said:
They said to him:
phrases.notes: The מלאכים are speaking to אברהם.

phrases.english: Do you really suspect us of being Arabs,
who bow down to the dust of their feet?
ישמעאל has already come out from him.
phrases.notes: Literally 'from him,' meaning אברהם. His own son ישמעאל acts that way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the rewards to a new explanation of the same פסוק about water
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מלאכים objected to being suspected of worshipping the dust of their feet, noting that ישמעאל, who comes from אברהם, is of that kind.

steps.title: What does 'in the heat of the day' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק about הקב"ה appearing to אברהם and asks what 'the heat of the day' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And ה׳ appeared to him by the trees of Mamre, as he sat at the opening of the tent in the heat of the day.' What does 'in the heat of the day' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new piece about אברהם by quoting a פסוק and asking about one phrase in it. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק adds a detail that seems unnecessary: that it was very hot. The גמרא wants to know why the תורה tells us about the weather.

keyTerms.meaning: In the heat of the day
The trees (terebinths) of Mamre, where אברהם lived
What is? (asks for the meaning of a word or phrase)

phrases.english: "And the Lord appeared to him by the terebinths of Mamre,
phrases.notes: בראשית 18:1

phrases.english: as he sat at the opening of the tent
in the heat of the day."
What is "in the heat of the day"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new piece of אגדה about אברהם, after the earlier pieces about his hospitality.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the פסוק mention that it was the heat of the day?

steps.title: It was the third day after אברהם's מילה
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא explains that הקב"ה came to visit אברהם on the third day after his מילה and made it very hot so guests would not trouble him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא said: That day was the third day after אברהם's מילה. הקב"ה came to ask how אברהם was doing. הקב"ה took the sun out of its cover so that this צדיק would not have to trouble himself with guests.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא answers the question. The heat was sent on purpose by הקב"ה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The third day after a מילה is the most painful one. הקב"ה visited the sick אברהם, and He made the day blazing hot so no travelers would be on the road. That way אברהם would not push himself to host guests while he was healing.

keyTerms.meaning: To ask after someone's welfare; here, to visit the sick
The Holy One, Blessed be He

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥama, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said:
That day was the third day
of Abraham's circumcision,

phrases.aramaic: וּבָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִשְׁאוֹל בְּאַבְרָהָם,
phrases.english: and the Holy One, Blessed be He, came to ask after Abraham's well-being.

phrases.aramaic: הוֹצִיא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא חַמָּה מִנַּרְתִּיקָהּ
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, took the sun out of its sheath
phrases.notes: Picture the sun shining with no cover at all, so the day became extremely hot.

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יַטְרִיחַ אוֹתוֹ צַדִּיק בְּאוֹרְחִים.
phrases.english: so that that righteous man would not trouble himself with guests.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The heat was sent by הקב"ה on the third day after the מילה so that no guests would come and trouble אברהם.

steps.title: אברהם sends אליעזר to look for guests
steps.stepSummary: אברהם sends אליעזר out to find guests. אליעזר finds no one, and אברהם does not believe him. The גמרא links this to a saying that slaves are not trustworthy.
steps.simpleTranslation: אברהם sent אליעזר to go outside. He went out and did not find anyone. אברהם said: I do not believe you. This is what people say there: slaves are not trustworthy.
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on. Even in pain and heat, אברהם wanted guests, so he sent his servant to look for them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הקב"ה's plan worked: no travelers were out. אברהם still did not trust אליעזר's report, and the גמרא points to a well-known saying that matches this.

phrases.english: He sent Eliezer to go outside.
He went out and did not find anyone.
He said: I do not believe you.
This is what they say there:
phrases.notes: "There" means ארץ ישראל. People there had this saying.

phrases.english: There is no trustworthiness in slaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story after הקב"ה made the day hot.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אברהם looked for guests even while in pain, and did not rely on his servant's report that none were there.

steps.title: אברהם goes out and finds הקב"ה at the door
steps.stepSummary: אברהם goes out himself and sees הקב"ה standing at the door. The גמרא shows this from the פסוק 'אל נא תעבר מעל עבדך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He himself went out and saw הקב"ה standing at the door. This is what is written: 'Please do not pass away from Your servant.'
steps.whatsHappening: אברהם checks for himself and finds הקב"ה at the entrance. The גמרא brings a פסוק to support this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק has אברהם asking someone not to leave him. The גמרא reads it as אברהם speaking to הקב"ה, which shows that הקב"ה was right there at the door.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what is written (connects the story to a פסוק)
Please do not pass away / leave

phrases.english: He himself went out

phrases.aramaic: חַזְיֵיהּ לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא דְּקָאֵי אַבָּבָא.
phrases.english: and saw the Holy One, Blessed be He, standing at the door.
This is what is written:
"Please do not pass away from Your servant."
phrases.notes: בראשית 18:3

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב: ״אַל נָא תַעֲבֹר מֵעַל עַבְדֶּךָ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: after not trusting אליעזר, אברהם goes out himself.
steps.raayaObject: That הקב"ה was standing at אברהם's door.

steps.title: Seeing אברהם's pain, it was not proper to stand there
steps.stepSummary: Seeing אברהם tying and untying his bandage, it was decided that standing over him was not proper. The גמרא connects this to the פסוק about three men standing over him and אברהם running to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once He saw that אברהם was tying and untying his bandage, He said: It is not proper to stand here. This is what is written: 'He lifted his eyes and saw, and behold, three men were standing over him, and he saw and ran toward them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story says that standing right over the hurting אברהם was not respectful, so they moved away. The גמרא brings a פסוק for this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק first says the men were standing over him, then says he ran to meet them. That suggests they moved away in between, and the next step explains exactly how.

phrases.english: Once He saw that he was tying and untying,
phrases.notes: אברהם was tying and untying the bandage on his מילה, which showed he was in pain.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר: לָאו אוֹרַח אַרְעָא לְמֵיקַם הָכָא.
phrases.english: He said: It is not proper conduct to stand here.
This is what is written:
"And he lifted up his eyes and saw,
and behold, three men were standing over him;
and he saw, and ran to meet them."
phrases.notes: בראשית 18:2

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story and ties it to the next פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That they moved away from standing over אברהם once they saw he was in pain.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 18:2, where the men stand over him and then he runs to them.

steps.title: How the men stood over him and he still ran to them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the פסוק: first the men stood over אברהם, and when they saw his pain they stepped away, so he then ran to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first they came and stood over him. When they saw that he was in pain, they said: It is not proper to stand here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how both parts of the פסוק fit together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If they were already standing over him, why did he need to run to them? Because they backed away when they saw his pain, so he ran to reach them.
steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק shows two stages: the guests stood over אברהם, then stepped back out of respect for his pain, and he ran to meet them.

phrases.english: At first they came and stood over him.
When they saw that he was in pain,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ: לָאו אוֹרַח אַרְעָא לְמֵיקַם הָכָא.
phrases.english: they said: It is not proper conduct to stand here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the wording of the פסוק quoted in step 33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the פסוק as two stages in time
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seems to contradict itself: the men stand over him, yet he runs to them.
steps.terutzMaskana: They first stood over him, then moved away when they saw his pain, and he ran to them.

steps.title: Who were the three men?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the three men in the פסוק were.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who are the three men?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the identity of the three visitors. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls them 'men', but the גמרא wants to know exactly who they were.

phrases.english: Who are the three men?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the three men mentioned in the פסוק from step 33.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the three men who visited אברהם.

steps.title: מיכאל, גבריאל and רפאל, each with a job
steps.stepSummary: The three men were the מלאכים מיכאל, גבריאל and רפאל. מיכאל came to bring news to שרה, רפאל to heal אברהם, and גבריאל to overturn סדום.
steps.simpleTranslation: They were מיכאל, גבריאל and רפאל. מיכאל came to bring the good news to שרה. רפאל came to heal אברהם. גבריאל went to overturn סדום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the three מלאכים and explains why each one came.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each מלאך had his own separate mission. That is why three came and not one.

phrases.english: Michael, Gabriel, and Raphael.
Michael, who came to bring news to Sarah;
Raphael, who came to heal Abraham;
Gabriel went to overturn Sodom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 35.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The three were מיכאל (news for שרה), רפאל (healing אברהם) and גבריאל (overturning סדום).

steps.title: But the פסוק says two מלאכים came to סדום
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if only גבריאל went to סדום, why does the פסוק say that two מלאכים came there?
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written: 'And the two מלאכים came to סדום in the evening'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last step with a פסוק that seems to disagree with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 36 said only גבריאל's job was סדום. The פסוק says two מלאכים arrived there, so it seems a second one also went.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is written! (opens a challenge from a פסוק)

phrases.english: But it is written:
"And the two angels came to Sodom in the evening"!
phrases.notes: בראשית 19:1

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 36's statement that only גבריאל went to סדום.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that only גבריאל went to סדום.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק says two מלאכים came to סדום, not one.

steps.title: מיכאל went along to save לוט
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that מיכאל went with גבריאל to סדום, but only to save לוט.
steps.simpleTranslation: מיכאל went with him to save לוט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Two went to סדום, but for different jobs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גבריאל still did the overturning. מיכאל came along only to rescue לוט, so the פסוק can say 'two מלאכים'.

phrases.english: Michael went along with him
to save Lot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 37.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a second, separate job to the second מלאך
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two מלאכים came to סדום, so both must have come to destroy it.
steps.terutzMaskana: מיכאל came only to save לוט. Only גבריאל overturned סדום.

steps.title: The פסוק says 'he overturned', so only one מלאך did it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports its answer: the פסוק says 'he overturned' in the singular, not 'they overturned', so only one מלאך destroyed the cities.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording fits this too, since it is written: 'And he overturned those cities.' It is not written 'and they overturned.' Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for its answer from the exact wording of another פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both מלאכים had destroyed סדום, the פסוק would say 'they overturned'. The singular 'he overturned' shows that only one did it, which fits מיכאל being there only to save לוט.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is precise too (supports what was just said)
Learn from this; conclude from it

steps.whatToRemember: Three מלאכים came to אברהם, each with one job. Two went on to סדום, but only גבריאל overturned it, as the singular 'ויהפך' shows. מיכאל was there to save לוט.

phrases.english: The wording is precise too,
as it is written: "And he overturned those cities,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 19:25

phrases.english: and it is not written "and they overturned."
Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 38 from the wording of a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That only one מלאך overturned סדום, while מיכאל came only to save לוט.

steps.title: Why did the מלאכים agree at once with אברהם but not with לוט?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא contrasts two hosting stories. With אברהם, the מלאכים agreed right away (״כן תעשה כאשר דברת״). With לוט, they first refused. The גמרא asks what makes the two cases different.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about אברהם, where the פסוק says: "So do, as you have said," and what is different about לוט, where the פסוק says: [the פסוק about לוט comes next]
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new question by comparing two stories: the מלאכים accepted אברהם's invitation immediately, but with לוט they held back. The פסוק about לוט is quoted right after this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both אברהם and לוט invited the same kind of guests, so we would expect the same reaction. Instead, the פסוקים show two different reactions: instant agreement with אברהם, and a refusal first with לוט. The גמרא wants a reason for this difference.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Used to ask why two similar cases are treated differently
With regard to, in the case of
"So do, as you have said": the מלאכים' answer to אברהם
As it is written (introduces a פסוק)

steps.confusionAlert: This line stops in the middle of the question. The פסוק about לוט and the גמרא's answer come at the start of the next amud, so don't look for the answer here yet.

phrases.english: What is different with regard to Avraham,
as it is written: "So do, as you have said,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 18:5. The מלאכים agree right away to stay and eat with אברהם.

phrases.english: and what is different with regard to Lot,
as it is written:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After identifying the מלאכים and their missions, the גמרא turns to a new detail in the two hosting stories: how the מלאכים responded to each invitation.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the מלאכים accepted אברהם's hospitality immediately but first refused לוט's.
